layouts.name: Gaydon Emissions Circuit
layouts.description: The University of Warwick 2001 research report reproduces the Rover Gaydon Emissions Circuit plan in Figure 3.10, page 68: the southwest hairpin, long former-runway straights, northern bend and bridge-end return. The manufacturer confirms the dedicated four-lane Emissions Circuit. Independent Environment Agency 2018 one-metre LiDAR intensity survey tiles locate the complete surviving pavement and its southwest end, excluding the shorter mid-runway reversal, handling roads, access and other test areas. The independently measured 6,302.9 m differs from the supplied 6,092 m by 210.9 m; neither it nor the historical course plan is fitted to the supplied scalar. All vertices follow the public survey. Native grid mosaic, source member hashes, crop transform, grayscale stretch and nearest-neighbor reprojection are pinned. This is reflected laser intensity, not colour photography. Historical lane selection, fine racing-line placement and later road modifications remain draft. Private timing data does not determine geometry Independently digitized aerial centerline: 6302.9 m. Direction, historical configuration and fine corner alignment remain draft; no course coordinates come from the comparison catalogue.
